chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, who said: Abū Yūsuf Ya'qūb ibn 'Abdillah, from the descendants of Ab Fāṭimah, narrated to me from Ismā'īl ibn Zayd, the freedman of 'Abdillah ibn Yaḥyā al-Kāhilī, from Abū 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) while he was in the Mosque of Kūfah and said, 'Peace be upon you, O Commander of the Believers, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.' He (peace be upon him) responded. The man said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I intend to go to the Farthest Mosque (Bayt al-Maqdis), so I wanted to bid you farewell.' He (peace be upon him) asked, 'What do you hope to gain by that?' The man said, 'The reward (al-faḍl), may I be sacrificed for you.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Sell your camel, eat your provisions, and pray in this mosque, for the obligatory prayer performed in it is a purified Hajj, and the recommended prayer is a purified 'Umrah.'

The blessings of it extend to twelve miles. Its right side is prosperity, and its left side is cunning. In its center is a spring of oil, a spring of milk, a spring of water for drinking for the believers, and a spring of water for purification for the believers.
The ark of Noah sailed from it, and Nasr, Yaghuth, and Ya'q were placed in it. Seventy prophets and seventy successors prayed in it, and I am one of them.

And he (peace be upon him) pointed to his chest with his hand, saying: 'No distressed person asks Allah for anything in it (the Mosque of Kūfah) regarding any of the needs, except that Allah answers him and relieves him of his distress.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards of praying in the Mosque of Kūfah compared to other mosques?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) advised a man traveling to the Farthest Mosque (Bayt al-Maqdis) to stay in Kūfah and pray there instead, equating the reward of obligatory and recommended prayers in Kūfah to a purified Hajj and 'Umrah. The narration highlights the spiritual merits of the Mosque of Kūfah, including its blessings, historical significance with prophets and successors, and the acceptance of supplications. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of Kūfah as a center of Imamate authority, where the presence of the Imams amplifies the spiritual weight of worship, offering a localized alternative to the pilgrimage to Jerusalem.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 18. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Abī Yūsuf Ya’qūb ibn ‘Abdillāh who was from the children of Abī Fāťimah, from Ismā’īl ibn Zayd servant of ‘Abdillāh ibn Yaḥyā Al-Kāhili, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

A man came to the Commander of the Believers (a.s.) in the Mosque of Kūfah and said, “Salām to you, O Commander of the Believers. May Allāh’s Mercy and His Blessings be upon you!” The Commander of the Believers (a.s.) answered his Salām. “May I sacrifice myself for you! I am leaving for the Mosque of Aqsā and I wanted to bid farewell to you,” the man said. The Commander of the Believers (a.s.) asked, “What do you hope to gain by going there?” The man said, “May I sacrifice myself for you! Rewards!”

The Commander of the Believers (a.s.) said: Sell your camel, spend your money, and pray in this mosque instead, for establishing obligatory prayers in this mosque is equal to performing a purified Hajj, and establishing recommended prayers in it is equal to performing a purified ‘Umrah.

The blessings of this mosque extend to a twelve mile (radius). The right side of this mosque is prosperity but its left side is cunning. In the middle of this mosque, there is a well of oil, a well of milk, a well of water for the believers to drink, and a well of water to purify the believers.

The ark of Nūḥ embarked from here and Nasr, Yaghūth, and Ya’ūq were placed here. The Commander of the Believers (a.s.) continued: Seventy prophets and seventy successors have prayed in this mosque, and I am one of them – and he pointed to his own chest.
No anguished person asks Allāh for anything in it (the Mosque of Kūfah) without Allāh granting (his request) and relieving him of his grief.
